style.vernacular: Low-rise Pacific capital: single- and two-storey painted concrete-block houses and shops with corrugated-iron roofs (red, green, blue, grey), timber houses on stilts, large whitewashed churches that dominate each village, a few Victorian-style timber buildings from the 19th century monarchy, and traditional oval thatched fale with curved roofs lashed with sennit (coconut-fibre) rope. Coconut palms, banyan, flame trees. Wall and roof colours are estimates from general knowledge: no retrievable source gave a colour palette.
style.ornament: Traditional fale: curved limpet-shell roof of branches tied with sennit and thatched with woven palm leaves on tree-trunk pillars, woven screens between ground and eaves; church walls sometimes painted freehand with crosses, flowers and ngatu (barkcloth) motifs; coral-limestone mound tombs and trilithon; stone then iron fences around royal sites.

sources.what: traditional fale: curved sennit-lashed thatched roof on trunk pillars with woven screens; church murals with ngatu motifs; stone langi and trilithon
wooden palace of 1867 by the waterfront, enclosed first by stone fence, later by a 3 m grid fence with iron-barred gates
